newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Crime and vengeance terrify Sierra Leone capital.
newsitem.headline: Crime and vengeance terrify Sierra Leone capital.

text.p: Hacked to death on the streets of Freetown a teenage boy on Wednesday became the latest victim of a wave of crime and vengeance in the anarchic atmosphere of Sierra Leone's capital, a month after a widely condemned coup.

Police on the scene said they believed the boy had been killed by a mob after they caught him breaking into a house -- his arms and head had been chopped off and one severed testicle placed in his mouth.
"I know the boy. He doesn't live in the area but he frequents it during the day. He has been leading gangs of boys who break into people's homes, looting them clean," said one bystander.

Local youths said they had formed into vigilante groups since a May 25 military coup by Major Johnny Paul Koroma toppled elected president Ahmed Tejan Kabbah in the impoverished former British colony on the West African coast.

The military rulers, now allied with the rebel foes they fought since 1991, face attacks by ethnic hunters militias which support Kabbah, as well as pressure from the region and the rest of the world to reinstate the ousted president.

Officials in regional giant Nigeria said a meeting would be held in Sierra Leone's neighbour Guinea on Thursday to discuss the coup. Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown on June 2, but widely expected further military action has not materialised.

Freetown residents say the arrival of more combatants in the city from the jungle interior, mixed with uncertainty over the future of Koroma's government, have spawned the terrifying wave of crime and gruesome popular punishment.

"In the East End there is no night life left," said a schoolteacher from the largely working class district that once hummed with evening activity of bars playing loud music and street sellers hawking food.
"People bolt their doors as soon as night falls ...and we are forced to sleep under our beds for fear of a knock on the door from armed men.
"If you refuse (to open) they shoot down the door and take what they want away. If you are lucky they rape you and if you are unlucky they kill you," she said.

State radio on Tuesday broadcast a message from the military rulers acknowledging that looting and killing continued in the city, whose pre-war population of 400,000 has more than doubled with the arrival of people displaced by fighting.

But promises of intensified patrols have done nothing to ease the minds of frightened citizens, and those who can are paying the $200 fare to escape to neighbouring Guinea or even Liberia -- barely emerged from its own civil war.
